images.title: Only 2s and 5s make 10s
images.purpose: Show that 10, 100 and 1000 are built only from 2s and 5s, so a denominator of 3 can never be grown into them.
images.composition: Three rows of small chips on the left two thirds of the frame and a single crossed out chip on the right third, with one short caption at the bottom.
exact_structure: Row 1: the text 10 = followed by 1 teal #0072B2 chip labelled 2 and 1 amber #E69F00 chip labelled 5.
Row 2: the text 100 = followed by 2 teal #0072B2 chips labelled 2 and 2 amber #E69F00 chips labelled 5.
Row 3: the text 1000 = followed by 3 teal #0072B2 chips labelled 2 and 3 amber #E69F00 chips labelled 5.
In all 12 chips on the left: 6 teal chips each labelled 2, 6 amber chips each labelled 5; a tiny × sign between neighbouring chips.
Right side: one larger vermilion #D55E00 chip labelled 3 with a grey #6B7280 diagonal strike line across it.
Bottom caption: 3 is not made of 2s and 5s.
rejection: any row with a chip count other than 2, 4 or 6
unequal numbers of 2 chips and 5 chips in a row
images.takeaway: Denominators made only of 2s and 5s can grow into 10, 100 or 1000; a denominator with 3 cannot.
images.description: Chips show 10 as 2 × 5, 100 as 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 and 1000 as 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5, beside a struck out chip labelled 3.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on why 10/3 has no equivalent fraction with denominator 10, 100 or 1000.
images.teaching_notes: Have students pair each teal 2 with an amber 5 to see each pair make a 10.

image_decisions.why: The chip picture explains why some divisions end and others need long division.
